correctness.rationale: The ternary bracket is reconstructed as [x,y,z]=x_3(y_3 z_2-y_2 z_3)e_2. The full Rota-Baxter identity on basis triples yields polynomial equations whose decisive factors partition all solutions by (a31,a32,a33). Each nonzero-bottom-row case is solved explicitly. The only characteristic-sensitive case is a31=a32=0,a33!=0, where 2a22^2a33=0 forces a22=0 away from characteristic two but disappears in characteristic two. Summing the disjoint strata gives the two formulas. Exhaustive enumeration over F2 and F3 independently matches 112 and 1107.

value.rationale: This is the explicit three-dimensional example used to ground a new deformation/cohomology framework for relative Rota-Baxter operators on 3-Leibniz algebras, so its finite-field moduli size is a natural exact invariant rather than an arbitrary parameter slice. The characteristic-two formula is structurally informative: it shows that naïvely reducing the source's characteristic-zero list misses an entire q^3(q-1)^2 family of operators. The result supplies both a closed point-count polynomial and a precise boundary mechanism for the jump.
